### 2.1 Carbohydrates (Glucose, Fructose & Glycosidic Linkage) (Carbohydrates)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **121 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Structure of D-glucose and D-fructose, cyclic hemiacetals, anomeric carbons ($\alpha/\beta$), reducing vs non-reducing sugars, and invert sugar.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{Sucrose (non-reducing)} \xrightarrow{\text{hydrolysis}} \text{D-(+)-glucose} + \text{D-(-)-fructose} \quad \text{(Invert sugar, levorotatory)}
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Sucrose is a NON-REDUCING sugar because both reducing groups (hemiacetal $-\text{OH}$ of glucose and hemiketal $-\text{OH}$ of fructose) are tied in glycosidic linkage.

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Hydrolysis of dextrorotatory sucrose produces a levorotatory mixture because fructose has a larger specific rotation ($-92.4^\circ$) than glucose ($+52.5^\circ$).

### 2.2 Amino Acids, Peptide Bonds & Nucleic Acids (Proteins & DNA)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **78 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Essential amino acids, zwitterionic dipolar character, protein denaturation, double-helix structure of DNA, and hydrogen-bonded base pairs.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
\text{Peptide linkage: } -\text{CO-NH}-, \quad \text{Zwitterion: } \text{H}_3\text{N}^+-\text{CHR}-\text{COO}^-, \quad \text{DNA: } \text{A}=\text{T}, \; \text{G}\equiv\text{C}
$$

#### Common Traps & JEE Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Denaturation destroys secondary, tertiary, and quaternary protein structures, but leaves the primary sequence (peptide bonds) INTACT.

synthesis.traps_and_pitfalls:
## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring JEE Mains Pitfalls in Biomolecules

### 1. Sign Convention & Vector Inversion Errors
Paper-setters frequently exploit sign confusion in energy and potential differences. Always write the fundamental thermodynamic / vector definition before substituting numerical values.

### 2. Unit System Discrepancies
Molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), SI vs CGS units, and micro/milli/nano multipliers (10^-3, 10^-6, 10^-9) account for over 35% of calculation mistakes in numerical type questions.

### 3. Boundary & Extreme Conditions
In transient circuits or limiting conditions (t=0+, t -> inf, infinite dilution, resonance), always check the asymptotic behavior of inductors, capacitors, and electrolyte mobility.

### 4. Direct Addition Fallacy
Never algebraically add intensive quantities (such as electrode potentials or AC component voltages) without accounting for electron weighting (n1*E1 + n2*E2 = n3*E3) or phasor vector geometry (V_total = sqrt(V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2)).
